clue.text: Document from academic men with an arts degree

parts.note: a prof is short for professor, a university academic
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers or men
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A paper produced by university men who hold an arts degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a standard printed form, a kind of document filled in to a set pattern.

clue.text: Rascal with sort of accent that's not British

indicators.note: 'sort of' says the letters of the rascal word are a kind of jumbled version of it

parts.note: a rascal is a rogue, a mischievous scoundrel

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who speaks with some foreign-sounding accent rather than a British one.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradman wrote the clue for ROGUE (bROGUE without B) and later admitted the slip. The entry ROUGE still parses: 'sort of' rearranges ROGUE, and rouge is a French word for blusher, a colour accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is a cosmetic used to put a colour accent on the cheeks, and its name is French rather than English.

clue.text: In favour of offer, European accommodates Conservative interdiction

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
a bid is an offer, as at auction

indicators.note: accommodates means the European word holds the Conservative letter inside it

parts.note: a Dane is a European, from Denmark

explanation.surface: Supporting a proposal, a European makes room for a Tory ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodates' turns the Dane into DANCE; the noun is rare but listed in dictionaries as an old word for forbidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbiddance is the act of forbidding, so it is a prohibition or interdiction.

clue.text: Once again load up, having moved car here outside front of garage

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters sit around the letter taken from garage
having moved says the letters of car and here are shifted around into a new order
front of picks the opening letter of the word garage

explanation.surface: Having driven the car round to the front of the garage, you fill it up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having moved' shuffles CAR HERE into RECHARE, and 'outside' places those letters around G, the first letter of 'garage'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recharge is to fill a battery or weapon with power or ammunition a second time, loading it up anew.

clue.text: They observe people in unexpected short stop in gaol

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of the following phrase turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Prison guards watch inmates during an unplanned brief halt in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' rearranges all fifteen letters of SHORT STOP IN GAOL; 'in' belongs to the fodder, not the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropologists study human societies and cultures, often by watching how people live.

clue.text: Comfort sun's brought to celebrity

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
an ace is a star performer, someone celebrated

explanation.surface: A famous person gets consolation from the warmth of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation, the relief or comfort given in distress.

clue.text: Quack gaining a name as bogus healer?

parts.note: quack as an adjective means fake, a sham

explanation.surface: A fraudulent doctor gets a reputation as a phoney healer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack' looks like the noun for a fake doctor but works as SHAM; the question mark flags that the definition is a sceptic's view of a tribal healer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and spirit medium, whom a sceptic might call a fake doctor.

clue.text: Left pair of spectacles in room

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of round spectacle lenses

explanation.surface: Someone has left their glasses in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: OO for spectacles is a visual convention: the two letters look like round lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: A loo is an informal British word for a toilet, the smallest room in the house.

clue.text: Discarded, apart from actors on stage?

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a play
aside means apart, to one side

explanation.surface: Thrown away, separately from the actors performing in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at a second reading: a cast aside is a stage remark made by the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cast aside is to be thrown away or abandoned as no longer wanted.

clue.text: Instructions irritate (having lots hard to get rid of)

parts.note: to rub is to chafe or irritate

indicators.note: to get rid of says the hard letter is dropped from the word for wealthy

parts.note: to be rich is to have lots of money
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Directions that annoy, laden with many difficult things to dispose of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get rid of' removes H from RICH, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a heading or set of directions, such as the instructions on an exam paper.

clue.text: Sitting by river, hate horrible restaurant

indicators.note: horrible suggests the word hate is mangled into a different order

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, flowing through York

explanation.surface: Seated beside a river, I loathe this awful eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges HATE into TEAH, followed by OUSE; 'Sitting by' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A teahouse is a café or small eating place where tea and light meals are served.

clue.text: Something distinctly elusive? It comes back to you

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: comes back means the word it is written backwards

explanation.surface: A game of tag: whoever is it returns to you.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is the old form of 'you'. 'comes back' reverses only 'It', not the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, the abominable snowman of the Himalayas, is a creature famously hard to find.

clue.text: Officer in a lair, having gone astray across boggy land

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters stretch over either side of the boggy land
having gone astray says the letters of a lair wander out of their order

parts.note: a marsh is wet, boggy ground

explanation.surface: A soldier in an animal's den who has wandered off over the swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone astray' shuffles A LAIR into AIRAL, and 'across' means those letters straddle the bog; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An air marshal is a senior officer rank in the Royal Air Force.

clue.text: Crook offering item that poses no danger at Christmas

definitions.meaning: a criminal who breaks into strongboxes

definitions.text: item that poses no danger at Christmas
definitions.meaning: a festive cracker that is harmless, one that is safe

explanation.surface: A criminal hands over a harmless festive novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart at Christmas dinner in Britain, going off with a small bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A safecracker is a criminal who breaks open safes, and a safe cracker is a harmless Christmas novelty.

clue.text: Traffic in front of clothes store — a matter of concern to business

definitions.text: a matter of concern to business

indicators.note: in front of places the trading word before the shop name

parts.note: to traffic is to trade or deal
Gap is a chain of clothing shops

explanation.surface: Congestion outside a fashion outlet worries the business community.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is a deficit between imports and exports, which worries commerce and economists.

clue.text: Copy procedure as rejigged

indicators.note: rejigged means the letters of procedure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Duplicate the method, as revised.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce something is to make a copy of it.

clue.text: Loud impertinence making one go mad

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
lip is cheek or insolence

explanation.surface: Noisy cheek drives someone crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is informal for losing one's temper or going crazy.

clue.text: Turn up as loony in agreement

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters of the phrase go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A mad person shows up, apparently agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuant means in accordance with something, as in pursuant to the agreement.

clue.text: Frank reveals love, something put down on paper

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
a pen is put down on paper to write

explanation.surface: A candid admission of love written in a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open means being candid and honest, hiding nothing.

clue.text: Rocket from restaurant critic maybe, penning article

indicators.note: penning means the diner word encloses the article, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: a restaurant critic is one example of someone who eats lunch out
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A food writer delivers a stinging review while writing an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing: A goes inside LUNCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A launcher is a device that fires rockets, here standing for the rocket's firing system by association.

clue.text: Brilliant to start with, then have failure

indicators.note: to start with places the slang word at the front of the answer

parts.note: def is slang for excellent or brilliant
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: A dazzling beginning, then a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeat is a loss or failure, as in a contest.

clue.text: Sing ever so badly to get coins

indicators.note: badly means the letters of the phrase are performed out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A busker performs dreadfully to collect money.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereigns are British gold coins once worth one pound.

clue.text: Sarah heading off to see friend

indicators.note: heading off says the pet name loses its first letter

parts.note: Sally is a familiar form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: A woman sets out to visit her pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the S from SALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or partner, someone on your side.

clue.text: Location with pavilion and house

definitions.meaning: ..., the London cricket ground famed for its pavilion
the House of ..., the upper chamber of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: A place with a pavilion and a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground; the House of Lords is the UK Parliament's upper chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's cricket ground has a famous pavilion, and the Lords is a parliamentary house.

clue.text: Member of old tribe with long hair, a predatory type

parts.note: the Huns were an ancient nomadic people
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: An ancient warrior with flowing locks who preys on others.
explanation.definitionFit: A huntress is a woman who hunts, a predator by pursuit.

clue.text: Member's book — first thing member has discarded

indicators.note: has discarded says a letter is taken out of the book word

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: first thing picks the opening letter of the second member

explanation.surface: A club member's book, with the first page thrown out by another member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first thing' picks M from 'member', and 'has discarded' removes it from TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe is a digit of the foot, and member can mean a limb or body part.

clue.text: Paul, the American singer and artist, in a foreign city

parts.note: Paul Anka is a North American pop singer
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A singer and a painter are found in a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, a city outside Britain.

clue.text: Fellow to come on scene after monarch's suffered setback?

definitions.text: Fellow to come on scene after monarch's suffered setback?

indicators.note: to come on scene after places the fellow word after the turned royal letters
suffered setback means the royal letters are turned backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man steps in after the king or queen has been laid low.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual monarch. The whole clue also describes the answer: a man who takes over when a monarch is incapacitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules on behalf of a monarch who is incapacitated, absent or too young.

clue.text: Ridicule? See it as retrograde and rebel

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the words it as are read in reverse

parts.note: to rise is to rebel, as in rising up

explanation.surface: Mock? Think of it as backward and revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' turns IT AS into SATI, followed by RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise is to mock or lampoon through wit and exaggeration.
